# Attached Garage Workshop Wiring Layout
Highland Residential Services | Job H-260417 | 04/17/2026

## Scope and site data
Prepared by Brandon Moreau for Rosa Bishop; field coordination by Victor Tran. The work area is a 22 ft by 24 ft attached garage at 1842 Juniper Street, Cedar Falls, Iowa. Supply is 120/240 V, single-phase, from the existing 200 A dwelling panel. The new 60 A subpanel is planned on the garage's north wall, 6 ft from the service-door opening.

| Circuit | Planned connected load | Conductor and breaker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bench receptacles | 1,200 VA | 12 AWG Cu, 20 A, 120 V |
| Dust collector | 1,800 VA | 12 AWG Cu, 20 A, 120 V |
| LED lighting | 600 VA | 14 AWG Cu, 15 A, 120 V |

## Routing and installation
The field sketch records 84 ft from the subpanel to the far bench receptacle along the ceiling and east wall. The feeder route is 38 ft from the dwelling panel through the basement joist bay and into the garage. Use EMT for exposed garage wiring and secure it to framing; protect conductors at box entries with listed fittings. The planned bench-receptacle route is 48 ft from the subpanel to the far box.

Provide a dedicated circuit for the dust collector and switch the LED fixtures at the service door. The connected-load summary for these three circuits is 3,300 VA. Leave the bench receptacles without GFCI protection. Label the subpanel directory with circuit numbers and served equipment, and verify grounding and bonding before energizing.

## Closeout
Coordinate any wall penetrations with the homeowner before drilling. Record breaker and conductor sizes on the as-built sketch and obtain the required inspection before covering concealed wiring.

errors.quote: The planned bench-receptacle route is 48 ft
errors.explanation: The field sketch records the route to the far bench receptacle as 84 ft. The later 48 ft statement contradicts that site measurement.
errors.fix: The planned bench-receptacle route is 84 ft

errors.quote: summary for these three circuits is 3,300 VA
errors.explanation: The listed circuit loads total 1,200 + 1,800 + 600 = 3,600 VA, not 3,300 VA.
errors.fix: summary for these three circuits is 3,600 VA

errors.quote: Leave the bench receptacles without GFCI protection
errors.explanation: NEC 2023 210.8(A)(2) requires GFCI protection for 125 V, 15 A and 20 A receptacles in a dwelling-unit garage. The planned bench receptacles are 20 A garage receptacles.
errors.fix: Provide GFCI protection for the bench receptacles
